content.text:
I submitted **index 29 (Mg 0.19 / Sb 0.81)** as the best composition. Its EQE was 0.0055%, the highest of the three I measured.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 22 | 0.61 | 0.0003 |
| 28 | 0.79 | 0.0045 |
| 29 | 0.81 | 0.0055 |

- **Why the Sb-rich end:** at 2.7 eV, MgO and MgSb₂O₆ have band gaps too wide to absorb the light. Only the Sb-rich oxides are likely to absorb, so I spent the first measurement on the most Sb-rich point.
- **Trend:** EQE rose with Sb content, and index 29 is the most Sb-rich point in the library, so nothing untested lies further along that direction.
- **XRD:** indices 26 and 29 show the same main phase, an Sb-oxide type. Index 29 has two extra weak peaks, which may mean slightly more of the light-absorbing Sb oxide.

**Limitations:**
- With only three merit measurements, I never measured anything below 61% Sb. I ruled out the Mg-rich half on band-gap reasoning, not on data.
- The trend from three points may not be smooth. A composition between indices 23 and 27 could still beat index 29, though the measured points don't suggest it.
- I used 2 of the 5 XRD measurements and did not run the phase-matching tool, so the phase identification is based only on peak positions.
